findings_qualitative.value: Redshifted narrow CO(2-1) absorption against the nuclear continuum shows cold clouds infalling at ~300 km/s, likely within ~100 pc of the black hole

evidence.quote: revealing ‘shadows’ cast by the molecular clouds as they move inward at about $\bm{300}$ kilometres per second towards the active supermassive black hole

claims.hypothesis: Cold molecular clouds fall toward the AGN in a clumpy accretion flow
claims.experiment: ALMA CO(2-1) spectrum extracted from beam on the continuum core
claims.result: Three narrow redshifted absorption lines at +240, +275, +335 km/s with sigma<~6 km/s
claims.finding: Cold clumpy clouds are infalling toward the black hole

evidence.quote: The data unambiguously show that cold molecular gas is falling inward along a line of sight that intersects the galaxy centre.

claims.hypothesis: Absorbers lie close to the black hole
claims.experiment: Compare with VLBA HI absorption and geometric/probability arguments
claims.result: HI infall velocity matches; gas confined to innermost 2 kpc in emission
claims.finding: Clouds are within tens to ~100 pc

evidence.quote: The infall velocity is the same as that for the cold molecular clouds seen in CO(2-1) absorption

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Clouds could be in non-circular bound orbits rather than radial infall; transverse velocity unknown

evidence.quote: If most of the clouds are instead locked in non-circular orbits around the black hole, the fuelling rate would depend on the gas angular momentum

limitations_admitted.value: Optical depth/covering factor uncertain due to beam contamination by emission

evidence.quote: the covering factor cannot be known with certainty
